Servlet 3.1 changeSessionId() is preferred over invalidate-and-recreate to preserve session attributes — appropriate ordering. Task 6 description (line 405) echoes the invariant.

Test discipline preserves regression-detection at the call-site granularity recommended in patterns.md.

Task 7 description (line 412): 'preserving anti-enumeration 404 mapping (uniform 404 for foreign-owned / soft-deleted / IllegalArgumentException on bad ObjectId hex).' Explicit enumeration of all three 404 cases including the IllegalArgumentException → 404 mapping that Round 1 flagged.

Lifts R5 from manual operator step to automated regression gate. Closes the silent-deserialization-corruption risk.

findings.title: Documentation polish — `How it works` CSRF prose names plain handler, contradicts Architecture section's XOR handler binding
findings.description: tech-spec.md line 29 (Architecture, source of truth) correctly specifies `XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler` paired with `CookieCsrfTokenRepository.withHttpOnlyFalse()` for BREACH mitigation. However, line 57 (`How it works` narrative prose) says: `MVC CsrfFilter invokes CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler.handle(request, response, deferredToken)` — uses the plain handler name without the `Xor` prefix. This is documentation drift, not a security regression because the Architecture binding is the source of truth and Task 3 (line 383) references `D15 CSRF handler choice` — but a future implementer scanning only the `How it works` section could misread the prose as endorsing the plain handler.
findings.impact: Implementer reading the `How it works` runtime-flow narrative could implement the plain `CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler` and miss XOR randomization, re-opening the BREACH attack surface. Code-reviewer at Task 14 / security-auditor at Task 15 should catch it, but the spec itself should be self-consistent.
findings.recommendation: Update tech-spec.md line 57 to read: `MVC CsrfFilter invokes XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler.handle(request, response, deferredToken)` so the prose matches Architecture line 29's binding. Single-word edit.
